plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch covariate
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw salmon-derived integer gene-level counts for 12000 genes x 12 human kidney samples (6 treated, 6 control), with two known processing batches balanced across conditions. Because the batch holds both conditions, the correct design puts batch as a fixed covariate alongside condition (DESeq2 design ~ batch + condition) rather than pre-adjusting counts, which would break the count model's mean-variance relationship. The pipeline runs: (1) blind-VST sample-structure QC to confirm no batch-driven separation dominates and no outlier sample, (2) a minimal count pre-filter, (3) DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage as the primary DE method, (4) an edgeR quasi-likelihood fit on the same design as an independent robustness check, reporting the overlap as the high-confidence gene set, (5) preranked fgsea on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and then Reactome and WikiPathways human collections (follow-up) since the gene identifiers in the counts matrix and all three collections are HGNC symbols and need no re-mapping, and (6) a consolidated report with diagnostics, thresholds, gene tables, enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record. No transcript-level (quant.sf) files are available, so no tximport/length-offset step is included — the analysis proceeds on the gene-level count matrix as provided.
